A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NEAR method and retain matching core experiments. The text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison. v1 has no appendix; v2's Appendix A is available in full.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 report the authors' recalculated NAS correlations and original molecular-potential and EMNIST experiments, including repeated-training results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original benchmark evaluations, comparative analyses, and diagnostic experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The NEAR score, CNN feature-map subsampling procedure, and iterative power-law layer-sizing method are unchanged. The new benchmark applications and approximation tests do not introduce a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix A.2 adds seven TransNAS-Bench-101-Micro tasks, including autoencoding, surface-normal prediction, semantic segmentation, room layout, and jigsaw, plus language-model evaluation on HW-GPT-Bench. These substantially broaden the retained classification and molecular-potential coverage.

E2.justification: v1's EMNIST activation/initialization experiment reports only NEAR scores alongside losses. v2 adds direct comparisons against Grad_norm, SNIP, GraSP, Fisher, SynFlow, Zen-Score, ZiCo, and MeCoopt for those same combinations (A.3, Table 11). The original NAS comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include perplexity correlations for 20,000 sampled small HW-GPT-Bench architectures, evaluation after 0/1/3/5/10 training epochs, pairwise-ordering probabilities, and controlled layer and feature-map sampling studies. Table 6 also extends the EMNIST architecture sweep to 280–200 neurons. Existing settings are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained layer-size and activation studies, v2 adds training-stage stability, pairwise-ranking analysis, inspection of the 100 worst predictions, layer-contribution analysis, and full-matrix versus subsampled-feature-map sensitivity tests (A.4–A.8). These address substantial new diagnostic questions.

E5.justification: The original 20-run means/standard deviations and 32/400 score repetitions remain. v2 adds Monte Carlo probability estimation from one million network pairs, random-subset averaging, and 10,000-iteration averages for feature-map comparisons. No confidence intervals or formal significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Original NAS and activation-selection table values are retained, while Tables 9–13 and Figures A.5–A.9 add substantial results. Table 11 reports NEAR's Kendall/Spearman correlations as 0.84/0.70 versus MeCoopt's 0.67/0.45. Table 6 additionally reports loss 0.363 ± 0.008 for the 280–200 EMNIST network.

T1.justification: A.5 newly defines a pairwise-ranking probability conditional on the networks' accuracy ordering. This is a limited mathematical addition associated with evaluation. The effective-rank and NEAR definitions, power-law sizing formulation, and existing mathematical reasoning remain unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's three contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free architecture ranking, layer-size estimation, and activation/initialization selection. Additional experiments support these claims without redefining their central scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive applicability and mechanism interpretations: parameter count remains stronger on HW-GPT-Bench, large networks dominate NEAR's worst prediction errors, layer contributions appear distributed, and subsampling preserves kernel/channel sensitivity. These extend v1's retained qualifications about training dynamics and unresolved close performance differences.

D1.justification: The reproducibility statement explicitly adds raw-data availability at the same Zenodo record; code and hyperparameter access were already disclosed in v1. Condensed activation-experiment captions omit some earlier wording about random initialization and input resampling per repetition.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for TransNAS-Bench-101, HW-GPT-Bench, GELU, and Mok et al.'s training-stage analysis, while removing the original MNIST recognition reference. The main related-work discussion and positioning among zero-cost proxies remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most main-text prose and the section sequence remain intact. v2 converts contribution and procedure lists into prose, removes the introductory roadmap, shortens captions, introduces the lMLP abbreviation, and organizes additional material under Appendix A and a reproducibility statement.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a single-column conference layout, relocates all four original figures to Appendix A.1, and merges v1 Tables 5–6 and 7–8 into paired comparison tables. It also adds five result tables and five diagnostic figures, substantially changing the visual organization.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked direct competing-proxy validation of hyperparameter selection and empirical validation of its CNN subsampling approximation. v2 addresses both gaps in A.3 and A.8, broadens task coverage, and adds informative stability and failure analyses. These substantially strengthen empirical credibility, including documenting where parameter count remains stronger. The modest loss of detail from shortened captions does not outweigh these gains.
